maya: Heads-up — nightly perf run shows a regression on seqlen-heavy latency for the 13B path. Not huge but consistent: +18% p50 on generated tokens. :eyes:

ryan: Ugh. Is this the torch.compile rollout? We saw some odd kernel picks last week.

maya: Possibly. Regression first appeared after we enabled compile+cuda-graph capture for the streaming path. Repro script attached.

maya: ```bash
# quick repro (docker image: rwd-infer/nightly)
python perf_repro.py --model redwood-13b --batch 1 --seqlen 1024 --warmup 10 --iter 50
# observe p50 vs baseline
```

danielle: Can you paste the nsys flame or kernel top? I want to see which kernels spiked.

maya: nvprof/nsys snapshot (trimmed):
```
% time  : own_time  : kernel
24.1%   :  1.34s    : cutlass_gemm_fp8_fwd
19.7%   :  1.10s    : flash_attn_fwd
14.2%   :  0.79s    : cudagraph_capture_overhead
10.9%   :  0.61s    : kv_cache_update
```
We used to see cutlass ~17% and flash_attn ~27% — now swapped and cudagraph_capture shows up.

ryan: Interesting — cudagraph_capture_overhead is new. Could be that torch.compile triggers a different capture boundary and we recompile a capture for seqlen buckets. That + a different kernel preference for the compiled graph could explain p50 shift.

danielle: Also note kv_cache_update at 10%. Did we change the KV layout? We recently tweaked the KV packing to optimize for seqlen < 512. If capture forces a static shape path, longer seqlens might force copies/spills.

maya: Good point. I ran a quick A/B: disabling cuda-graph capture makes p50 go back to baseline. So capture interplay is the culprit.

ryan: Actionable experiments: (1) run with torch.compile disabled to confirm, (2) run capture with explicit dynamic capture (capture_stream=False style), (3) force kernel autotuner to re-profile for the compiled graph.

danielle: I tried (1) and (3) locally. Forcing re-autotune on compiled graphs requires clearing the kernel-profile cache per-compiled-graph id; here's the snippet I used: 
```
# pseudo
autotuner.clear_cache(graph_id)
autotuner.run_profile(graph, sample_shapes=[(1,1024)])
```
It brought cutlass back into the hot path and removed cudagraph_capture_overhead, p50 improved but still +6%.

maya: Hmm still +6% — might be batching heuristics interacting. The runtime seems to prefer larger tile sizes for compiled graphs which increases warp occupancy but hurts short-token steady-state latency.

ryan: Can we reproduce with a minimal model step to isolate KV behavior? If KV update is adding copies when capture is present, that explains extra tail. Try toggling kv_cache_alloc_strategy to "dynamic" vs "static".

maya: I ran toggles. Results: static alloc -> +12% p50, dynamic alloc -> +4% p50. So capture makes our static allocator do extra memcopies for seqlen 1024.

danielle: That suggests two fixes: (A) change capture region boundaries to avoid pinning sequence-length-specific allocations (B) make autotuner profile compiled graphs in the same runtime config as capture to pick kernels that favor steady-state latency.

ryan: Agreed. I'll open a quick PR to: 1) add autotune hook post-torchcompile, 2) make capture detect current kv allocator and pick a generic allocation plan, 3) add a runtime flag --capture-avoid-static-kv for e2e testing.

maya: Please also add a regression test in nightly that runs batch=1 seqlen=1024 for 1000 tokens and fails if p50 increases >8% compared to baseline image.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-3821: "torch.compile + cuda-graph: kernel autotune & kv allocation mismatch causing p50 regression". Assigned to @ryan and @danielle. :white_check_mark:

perf-bot: Nightly diff attached: https://perf.rwd/compare/1852502468 shows breakdown by kernel. Baseline vs nightly.

ryan: I'll iterate on the PR today. Thanks for hunting this down maya and danielle.

maya: Thanks — I can help validate fixes on dedicated infra later tonight. :party_parrot:
